label: History
value: Billina was cast ashore
unit: Billina was cast ashore with Dorothy Gale in a chicken coop after a storm at sea. Upon arriving on the beach of the Land of Ev, Dorothy renamed her Billina and discovered she could talk in fairy lands. Billina uncovered the golden key that unlocked Tiktok's storage room and accompanied Dorothy through Ev, advising her and warning her about Wheelers. When taken captive by Princess Langwidere, Billina was put into a chicken house, where she fought and conquered the local rooster before being freed by Ozma's party. During the expedition to rescue the royal family of Ev from the Nome King, Billina hid under the throne and overheard the King revealing that the enchanted royals were purple ornaments. She subsequently used this secret to disenchant the entire royal family of Ev, as well as Ozma and her followers. She also accidentally laid an egg in the throne room, discovering that eggs are deadly poison to Nomes, which allowed her group to force the Nome King's compliance. Following the adventure, Billina was rewarded with a jewel necklace by the new King of Ev and chose to settle permanently in the Land of Oz due to its superior bugs. She later hatched ten chicks in Oz, naming every single one of them 'Dorothy', and attended Princess Ozma's birthday celebration with her brood.

unit: Billina was cast ashore with Dorothy Gale in a chicken coop after a storm at sea. Upon arriving on the beach of the Land of Ev, Dorothy renamed her Billina and discovered she could talk in fairy lands. Billina uncovered the golden key that unlocked Tiktok's storage room and accompanied Dorothy through Ev, advising her and warning her about Wheelers. When taken captive by Princess Langwidere, Billina was put into a chicken house, where she fought and conquered the local rooster before being freed by Ozma's party. During the expedition to rescue the royal family of Ev from the Nome King, Billina hid under the throne and overheard the King revealing that the enchanted royals were purple ornaments. She subsequently used this secret to disenchant the entire royal family of Ev, as well as Ozma and her followers. She also accidentally laid an egg in the throne room, discovering that eggs are deadly poison to Nomes, which allowed her group to force the Nome King's compliance. Following the adventure, Billina was rewarded with a jewel necklace by the new King of Ev and chose to settle permanently in the Land of Oz due to its superior bugs. She later hatched ten chicks in Oz, naming every single one of them 'Dorothy', and attended Princess Ozma's birthday celebration with her brood.

label: History
value: The Braided Man originally lived on top of the earth.
unit: The Braided Man originally lived on top of the earth before establishing his factory in a cave halfway up Pyramid Mountain, located between the Invisible Valley and the Country of the Gargoyles. There he spent many years manufacturing products such as Assorted Flutters for flags and Rustles for ladies' gowns. When Dorothy and the Wizard encountered him in his cave, he invited them into his shop and offered them his goods. Finding that he had ribbons of every color except blue, Dorothy gave him a blue hair-ribbon from her suit-case, which made him deeply happy, and in return he insisted on gifting them boxes of flutters and rustles. Later, he was invited to Princess Ozma's birthday celebration in the Land of Oz. He brought a box of his finest flutters as a birthday gift for Ozma and walked in the birthday procession alongside the Candy Man.

label: Appearance
value: Button-Bright is a small, chubby-faced boy.
unit: Button-Bright is a small, chubby-faced boy with pretty curls and big, blue, earnest eyes. For Ozma's banquet, he was outfitted in a blue-and-gold satin suit. During part of his journey, he was temporarily transformed by King Renard IV to have a hairy fox's head with pointed ears, sharp nose, and keen little eyes.

label: History
value: Button-Bright got lost from home.
unit: Button-Bright got lost from home and was found digging a hole under a chestnut tree by Dorothy, Toto, and the shaggy man. He joined them on their travels, attracted to the shaggy man by the Love Magnet. Upon entering Foxville, King Renard IV deemed him exceptionally clever and conferred a fox's head upon him. Continuing their journey through Dunkiton, the Musicker's valley, and the Scoodlers' cave—where he narrowly escaped being made into soup—he eventually reached the edge of the Deadly Desert and crossed it in a sand-boat built by Johnny Dooit. Upon entering the Land of Oz, he fell into the Truth Pond, which instantly restored his original human head. He travelled with his companions to Nick Chopper's tin castle and onward to the Emerald City, where he met Princess Ozma and attended her grand birthday celebration. At the end of the festivities, he requested to go home, and the Wizard sent him back to his family safely inside a giant, durable bubble.

label: History
value: The Cowardly Lion met Dorothy Gale
unit: The Cowardly Lion first met Dorothy Gale, the Scarecrow, and the Tin Woodman when he bounded from a forest and attacked them, though he quickly confessed his cowardice and joined their journey to ask the Great Oz for courage. During their travel to the Emerald City, he carried his companions over deep chasms, faced the terrifying Kalidahs, and swam across a river to save their raft. While running through a field of deadly poppies, he fell asleep from the scent and was rescued by thousands of field mice organized by the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman. Upon reaching Oz, the Wizard demanded the death of the Wicked Witch of the West before granting his request. Sent to the Winkie Country, the Lion was captured by Winged Monkeys, imprisoned, and threatened with starvation by the Witch, but Dorothy secretly fed him at night until she melted the Witch. After returning to Oz and discovering the Wizard was a humbug, the Lion drank a potion provided by Oz, which he believed granted him true courage. He accompanied Dorothy to the Land of the South, along the way defeating a giant spider-monster and being chosen as King of the Forest by its animal inhabitants. Later, he joined Princess Ozma's expedition to the Land of Ev and the Nome King's underground kingdom, where he repeatedly braved the Iron Giant's pounding hammer to carry Ozma's army to safety. He subsequently became a faithful vassal and royal chariot-puller alongside his companion, the Hungry Tiger, serving Princess Ozma and guarding the Royal Palace of Oz.

During their travel to the Emerald City, he carried his companions over deep chasms, faced the terrifying Kalidahs, and swam across a river to save their raft. While running through a field of deadly poppies, he fell asleep from the scent and was rescued by thousands of field mice organized by the Scarecrow and Tin Woodman. Upon reaching Oz, the Wizard demanded the death of the Wicked Witch of the West before granting his request. Sent to the Winkie Country, the Lion was captured by Winged Monkeys, imprisoned, and threatened with starvation by the Witch, but Dorothy secretly fed him at night until she melted the Witch. After returning to Oz and discovering the Wizard was a humbug, the Lion drank a potion provided by Oz, which he believed granted him true courage. He accompanied Dorothy to the Land of the South, along the way defeating a giant spider-monster and being chosen as King of the Forest by its animal inhabitants. Later, he joined Princess Ozma's expedition to the Land of Ev and the Nome King's underground kingdom, where he repeatedly braved the Iron Giant's pounding hammer to carry Ozma's army to safety. He subsequently became a faithful vassal and royal chariot-puller alongside his companion, the Hungry Tiger, serving Princess Ozma and guarding the Royal Palace of Oz.

label: History
value: Dorothy lived on a quiet farm in Kansas
unit: Dorothy lived on a quiet farm in Kansas with her uncle and aunt until a powerful cyclone carried her farmhouse to the Land of Oz, accidentally crushing the Wicked Witch of the East upon landing. Guided by the Witch of the North to seek the Great Oz in the Emerald City, she put on the Witch's silver shoes and set off on the yellow brick road, befriending the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion along the way. After destroying the Wicked Witch of the West with a bucket of water, she discovered Oz was a humbug, but eventually made her way back home to Kansas using the silver shoes. On a subsequent sea voyage with Uncle Henry, Dorothy was washed overboard in a storm alongside a yellow hen named Billina, eventually leading her to free the royal family of Ev and defeat the Nome King with the help of Ozma and her Oz friends. Later, after being trapped underground during a California earthquake, she navigated strange subterranean realms alongside her kitten Eureka, her cousin Zeb, and the Wizard before being magically transported back to Oz and subsequently returned to Kansas. During another journey, guided by the Shaggy Man, she met Button-Bright and Polychrome, traveling through various lands to attend Princess Ozma's birthday celebration in the Emerald City, where she was granted the title of Princess before returning home once more.

Guided by the Witch of the North to seek the Great Oz in the Emerald City, she put on the Witch's silver shoes and set off on the yellow brick road, befriending the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion along the way. After destroying the Wicked Witch of the West with a bucket of water, she discovered Oz was a humbug, but eventually made her way back home to Kansas using the silver shoes. On a subsequent sea voyage with Uncle Henry, Dorothy was washed overboard in a storm alongside a yellow hen named Billina, eventually leading her to free the royal family of Ev and defeat the Nome King with the help of Ozma and her Oz friends. Later, after being trapped underground during a California earthquake, she navigated strange subterranean realms alongside her kitten Eureka, her cousin Zeb, and the Wizard before being magically transported back to Oz and subsequently returned to Kansas. During another journey, guided by the Shaggy Man, she met Button-Bright and Polychrome, traveling through various lands to attend Princess Ozma's birthday celebration in the Emerald City, where she was granted the title of Princess before returning home once more.

She accompanied Dorothy, Zeb, Jim the Cab-Horse, and the Wizard through various underground realms, often horrifying her companions by demanding to eat the Wizard's nine tiny piglets. When the party was imprisoned by the wooden Gargoyles, Eureka helped locate their detachable wings, enabling their escape. After reaching the Land of Oz, Eureka was accused of murder when Princess Ozma's pet white piglet vanished. She was put on trial in the Throne Room, where she treated the proceedings with defiance and sarcasm. When a trick by the Wizard to save her was ruined by her own outspokenness, Eureka finally revealed that she had merely hidden the piglet inside a pink vase for fun. Due to the disgrace following her attempt to harm the piglet, she was confined to Dorothy's room until Ozma wished both Dorothy and Eureka back to Kansas using the Magic Belt.

label: History
value: King Evoldo of Ev sold Evardo to Roquat the Nome King
unit: Evardo's father, King Evoldo of Ev, sold him alongside his mother and nine siblings to Roquat the Nome King in exchange for a long life. The Nome King transformed Evardo and his family into purple ornaments to decorate the rooms of his underground palace. Billina the yellow hen eventually discovered the secret of the purple ornaments and correctly guessed Evardo, restoring him to his true form along with his mother and siblings. After returning to the Land of Ev, the Queen introduced the fifteen-year-old Evardo to their subjects, placing a crown and ermine robe upon him and proclaiming him King Evardo Fifteenth. Following his coronation, he went to see if he could find cake in the royal pantry. Later, Evardo and his family traveled to the Emerald City to attend Princess Ozma's birthday banquet, presenting her with a diadem of diamonds set in radium.

label: History
value: King Evoldo sold his family to the Nome King.
unit: After King Evoldo sold his family to the Nome King, Prince Evring was transformed into a purple kitten ornament and kept in the underground palace. During the rescue mission to free the royal family of Ev, Dorothy touching the purple kitten ornament restored him to his true form. After being freed, he held Dorothy's hand in the throne room and offered her a home in Ev. During the return journey, he rode on the Sawhorse alongside Dorothy and unintentionally kept the Tin Woodman in his pocket in the form of a small green tin whistle he had picked up in the palace. When Billina touched the whistle and spoke the magic word, the Tin Woodman was restored to his normal self. Evring then safely returned home to the Land of Ev with his mother and siblings.

label: History
value: Glinda established her rule in the South Country of Oz.
unit: Glinda established her rule in the South Country of Oz, holding court from a castle on the edge of the desert upon a throne of rubies. When Dorothy Gale arrived seeking a way back to Kansas, Glinda instructed her on the power of her Silver Shoes and used the Golden Cap to return Dorothy's companions to their desired homes before freeing the Winged Monkeys. Later, when the Scarecrow sought her aid against General Jinjur's revolt, Glinda researched her historical library, deduced that the true heir to the Emerald City was Princess Ozma, and marched her all-female army to capture old Mombi. Glinda outmaneuvered Mombi's magical transformations, captured her, forced her to confess that Tip was Princess Ozma, and oversaw the restoration of Ozma to her rightful form and throne. She subsequently assisted Ozma in overcoming threats such as the Nome King, provided counsel, gifted a magic carpet to cross the desert, and welcomed Dorothy and her friends back on their various visits to Oz.

label: Personality
value: The Hungry Tiger has a fierce appearance.
unit: Despite his fierce appearance and his frequent insistence that he longs to eat fat babies, the Hungry Tiger is governed by a strict conscience that prevents him from ever harming innocent living creatures. He feels that acting cruelly would make him a bad tiger according to his nature, yet he chooses to remain moral even though it means suffering constant unsatisfied hunger. label: History
value: The Hungry Tiger left his forest life.
unit: The Hungry Tiger left his forest life and teamed up with his friend, the Cowardly Lion, because his conscience prevented him from devouring living creatures as tigers normally do. He accompanied the Cowardly Lion to the Emerald City to see Princess Ozma and volunteered to pull her golden chariot alongside the Lion during the expedition to the Land of Ev and the Nome King's realm. During the journey, he carried Dorothy Gale on his back past the giant swinging hammer and repeatedly braved the hammer to help carry Ozma's officers to safety. At the Nome King's underground palace, he guarded Dorothy and Prince Evring, threatening the Nome soldiers with his sharp teeth. Upon returning to the Emerald City, he devoured a massive feast in celebration. Later, he served as a juror during the trial of Eureka the kitten for the alleged murder of a piglet and joined the Cowardly Lion in defending the Sawhorse from Jim the Cab-horse. He later welcomed Dorothy, the shaggy man, Button-Bright, and Polychrome to Oz when sent by Ozma to escort them in her royal chariot to her birthday celebration.

label: History
value: Tip built Jack out of wood.
unit: Tip built Jack out of wood and a carved pumpkin head to scare the witch Mombi, but Mombi instead used him to test her newly acquired Powder of Life, bringing Jack to life. Tip rescued Jack from Mombi's stable and took him on a journey toward the Emerald City. Along the way, Tip brought a Saw-Horse to life so Jack could ride it and spare his weak joints. After arriving in the Emerald City ahead of Tip, Jack met the Scarecrow and became his friend. During the rebellion led by General Jinjur, Jack escaped the city with Tip, the Scarecrow, and the Saw-Horse. When the group was trapped on the palace roof, Tip used the remaining Powder of Life to animate the Gump, allowing them to fly away. After Tip was restored to her true identity as Princess Ozma, Jack remained with her in the Emerald City. He eventually settled in a pumpkin field in the Winkie Country, where he built a house inside a giant pumpkin and farmed pumpkins to provide replacement heads when his old ones decayed. He later attended Ozma's birthday celebration in the Emerald City, presenting her with a necklace of carolite-set pumpkin seeds.

During the rebellion led by General Jinjur, Jack escaped the city with Tip, the Scarecrow, and the Saw-Horse. When the group was trapped on the palace roof, Tip used the remaining Powder of Life to animate the Gump, allowing them to fly away. After Tip was restored to her true identity as Princess Ozma, Jack remained with her in the Emerald City. He eventually settled in a pumpkin field in the Winkie Country, where he built a house inside a giant pumpkin and farmed pumpkins to provide replacement heads when his old ones decayed. He later attended Ozma's birthday celebration in the Emerald City, presenting her with a necklace of carolite-set pumpkin seeds.

label: History
value: Jim was pulling a buggy
unit: Jim was pulling a buggy driven by Zeb with Dorothy Gale as a passenger when an earthquake caused them to fall into a chasm into the underground Land of the Mangaboos. Upon falling into a fairy realm, Jim gained the ability to speak and walked on air down to the glass city. After eating rainbow grass in the vegetable gardens, he was banished alongside Eureka and nine tiny piglets by the Mangaboo Princess to the Black Pit. He fought off the vegetable people with his iron-shod hoofs before being reunited with Dorothy, Zeb, and the Wizard, who harnessed him to pull the buggy through mountain tunnels into the Valley of Voe. Threatened by invisible bears, Jim's hoofs were coated with magic leaves so he could pull the buggy over the river safely. Traveling through the Country of the Gargoyles, Jim flew using wooden wings wired to his harness to escape to a dark cavern. He was transported to the Emerald City of Oz by Princess Ozma's magic, where he was given a grand palace room and fed raw oatmeal. He met the Sawhorse, Cowardly Lion, and Hungry Tiger, but grew jealous of the Sawhorse during a race and kicked him, causing the Tiger to tackle him in response. Realizing he and Zeb did not belong in a fairyland, Jim requested to return home, and Ozma sent him and Zeb back to Hugson's Ranch.

Threatened by invisible bears, Jim's hoofs were coated with magic leaves so he could pull the buggy over the river safely. Traveling through the Country of the Gargoyles, Jim flew using wooden wings wired to his harness to escape to a dark cavern. He was transported to the Emerald City of Oz by Princess Ozma's magic, where he was given a grand palace room and fed raw oatmeal. He met the Sawhorse, Cowardly Lion, and Hungry Tiger, but grew jealous of the Sawhorse during a race and kicked him, causing the Tiger to tackle him in response. Realizing he and Zeb did not belong in a fairyland, Jim requested to return home, and Ozma sent him and Zeb back to Hugson's Ranch.

label: History
value: Johnny Dooit appeared at the edge of the Deadly Desert.
unit: Johnny Dooit appeared at the edge of the Deadly Desert after the shaggy man summoned him using the Love Magnet. Upon learning that Dorothy and her companions needed to cross the desert to reach the Land of Oz, he opened his copper tool-chest and rapidly built a functional sand-boat out of a felled tree, canvas, and ropes. After providing instructions on how to sail it, he snapped his chest shut and vanished instantly to continue his work elsewhere in the world. He later attended Princess Ozma's birthday celebration in the Emerald City, where he participated in the banquet and grand procession. During the festivities, he demonstrated his skills by constructing a flying machine on stage, which he used to fly away alongside his tool-chest after bidding farewell.

label: History
value: King Dox ruled over Foxville
unit: King Dox ruled over Foxville when Dorothy Gale, the shaggy man, Button-Bright, and Toto were escorted to his palace by his captain. During their audience, the King was so delighted by Button-Bright's clever responses that he used magic to transform the boy's head into that of a fox. He hosted the travelers for dinner and took them to a local theater performance, refusing to allow Aesop's fables to be mentioned in his presence. Before his guests departed the next morning, he asked Dorothy to obtain an invitation for him to Princess Ozma's birthday party in the Emerald City. He later traveled to the Land of Oz to attend the celebration, where he strutted around the Throne Room, kneeled at Dorothy's feet upon learning she was a Princess of Oz, sat at the animals' banquet table, and eventually struck up a friendship with King Kik-a-bray of Dunkiton.

label: Appearance
value: Princess Langwidere possesses a collection of thirty exchangeable heads.
unit: Princess Langwidere possesses a collection of thirty exchangeable heads—one for each day of the month—stored in velvet-lined cupboards inside a private cabinet. Each head features different hair, eyes, and facial features; for instance, head No. 9 has auburn hair and hazel eyes, while head No. 17 has glossy black hair, dark eyes, and a pearl-and-white complexion. The only constant mark by which her subjects can recognize her is a carved, blood-red ruby key attached to a chain on her left wrist.

label: History
value: Princess Langwidere resided in a wing of the royal palace of Ev.
unit: Princess Langwidere resided in a wing of the royal palace of Ev, where she spent her days playing mandolin and admiring her various heads in a room composed entirely of mirrors. Because her uncle King Evoldo had sold the royal family to the Nome King, she took money from the treasury and was the nearest approach to a ruler Ev had. When Dorothy Gale visited her, Langwidere insisted on exchanging heads with Dorothy. Upon Dorothy's refusal, the Princess ordered her army to lock Dorothy in the North Tower. Soon after, Princess Ozma of Oz arrived with her party and forced Langwidere to release Dorothy. Langwidere declined to join the expedition to rescue the royal family from the Nome King because she disliked heat and wished to admire her heads. After the royal family was rescued, Queen Evmar permitted Langwidere to retain her rooms and cabinet of heads for life, relieving her of all royal duties.

label: History
value: Mombi lived in the northern Gillikin region of Oz
unit: Mombi lived in the northern Gillikin region of Oz and raised a boy named Tip, forcing him to work around her farm while secretly practicing sorcery. After obtaining the Powder of Life from a crooked wizard, she tested it on a pumpkin-headed dummy Tip had created to scare her, bringing Jack Pumpkinhead to life. Intending to transform Tip into a marble statue as punishment for spying on her, she was outwitted when Tip fled that night taking Jack and the Powder of Life with him. Mombi then allied with General Jinjur's Army of Revolt to stop Tip and his companions, casting magical illusions to impede their journey. When Glinda marched on the Emerald City to capture her, Mombi repeatedly transformed herself and others into different shapes—including Jellia Jamb, a rose, a shadow, an ant, and a griffin—in an attempt to escape. Glinda eventually caught her on the desert borders with a golden thread. Brought to Glinda's tent, Mombi was compelled by threat of death to speak the truth, revealing that she had transformed Princess Ozma into Tip. After agreeing to give up her magic to save her life, Mombi performed an incantation over a herb fire that restored Tip to her true form as Princess Ozma.

Intending to transform Tip into a marble statue as punishment for spying on her, she was outwitted when Tip fled that night taking Jack and the Powder of Life with him. Mombi then allied with General Jinjur's Army of Revolt to stop Tip and his companions, casting magical illusions to impede their journey. When Glinda marched on the Emerald City to capture her, Mombi repeatedly transformed herself and others into different shapes—including Jellia Jamb, a rose, a shadow, an ant, and a griffin—in an attempt to escape. Glinda eventually caught her on the desert borders with a golden thread. Brought to Glinda's tent, Mombi was compelled by threat of death to speak the truth, revealing that she had transformed Princess Ozma into Tip. After agreeing to give up her magic to save her life, Mombi performed an incantation over a herb fire that restored Tip to her true form as Princess Ozma.

label: Appearance
value: Nome King is a fat little man.
unit: He is a fat little man clothed in gray-brown garments that match the exact rock color of his throne. His face, bushy hair, and flowing beard are also rock-colored, giving him a striking resemblance to Santa Claus. He wears no crown, and his main adornment is a broad, jewel-studded belt that encircles his fat body.

label: Personality
value: The Nome King initially appears jolly.
unit: The Nome King initially appears jolly, friendly, and good-humored, laughing until he shakes like jelly. However, beneath his courteous and smiling exterior lies a cunning, deceitful, and tyrannical nature. When crossed or outwitted, he flies into violent, furious rages, revealing a malicious and vengeful disposition.

label: History
value: King Roquat of the Rocks bought the Queen of Ev from King Evoldo.
unit: King Roquat of the Rocks bought the Queen of Ev and her ten children from King Evoldo, transforming them into bric-a-brac to decorate his underground palace. When Princess Ozma of Oz arrived with an army and companions to rescue the royal family, the Nome King pretended friendliness and offered a guessing game, tricking Ozma, the Tin Woodman, and many soldiers into failed guesses that turned them into ornaments as well. His plans were ruined when Billina the yellow hen discovered the secret to the enchantments and laid an egg in his throne room, terrifying the egg-phobic monarch. During the chaos, Dorothy Gale unbuckled his powerful magic belt and took it. Stripped of his magic power, the Nome King failed to prevent the escape of his captives and was left defeated on his throne, though he later continued to harbor plans to capture the Emerald City.

When Princess Ozma of Oz arrived with an army and companions to rescue the royal family, the Nome King pretended friendliness and offered a guessing game, tricking Ozma, the Tin Woodman, and many soldiers into failed guesses that turned them into ornaments as well. His plans were ruined when Billina the yellow hen discovered the secret to the enchantments and laid an egg in his throne room, terrifying the egg-phobic monarch. During the chaos, Dorothy Gale unbuckled his powerful magic belt and took it. Stripped of his magic power, the Nome King failed to prevent the escape of his captives and was left defeated on his throne, though he later continued to harbor plans to capture the Emerald City.

label: History
value: Ozma was stolen as an infant from her father
unit: Ozma was stolen as an infant from her father, the King of Oz, and hidden away with the witch Mombi, who transformed her into a boy named Tip. After growing up as Tip, she was restored to her true form through Glinda's intervention and installed as the rightful Queen of the Emerald City. As ruler, she appointed the Woggle-Bug as Public Educator, took the Sawhorse as her personal mount, and ruled with wisdom and justice. Later, learning that the royal family of Ev were held captive by the Nome King, she led an expedition across the desert on a magic carpet provided by Glinda. In the underground palace of the Nome King, she risked her own freedom in an attempt to guess which ornaments were the transformed royal family, but was herself turned into a green grasshopper ornament until rescued by Billina. Upon returning safely to Oz, she established a bond with Dorothy Gale, agreeing to monitor her through a Magic Picture and rescue her whenever signaled. She welcomed the Wizard of Oz back to the Emerald City, appointing him Official Wizard, and later hosted a grand birthday celebration on the 21st of her birth month, attended by notable figures from across Fairyland.

label: Personality
value: Polychrome is cheerful.
unit: Polychrome is cheerful, gentle, and affectionate, placing her trust quickly in new companions. She is exceptionally fond of dancing and loves to flit about constantly rather than stay still. She dislikes unpleasant noises like braying and finds the cold, hard earth unfamiliar compared to her home in the sky. She easily feels the chill when away from sunlight or activity, yet remains polite and charming to everyone she meets.

label: History
value: Polychrome was dancing on the rays of her father's rainbow.
unit: While dancing on the rays of her father's rainbow, Polychrome slid off the end to the ground, and was stranded when the rainbow lifted away. She met Dorothy Gale, Toto, the shaggy man, and Button-Bright on a road, agreeing to travel with them to the Emerald City in hopes that Princess Ozma could return her to the sky. Along the way, she navigated past the Musicker, survived capture by the Scoodlers, and crossed the dangerous desert on a sand-boat. Upon reaching the Land of Oz, she visited the Tin Woodman's castle, Jack Pumpkinhead's home, and the Emerald City, where she met Princess Ozma and was treated as an honored guest. At Princess Ozma's birthday banquet, Polychrome performed her mesmerizing Rainbow Dance to the delight of all the guests. During the festivities, Santa Claus promised to inform her father of her location, and shortly afterward a rainbow descended, allowing her to dance up its curve and reunite with her family.

label: History
value: Santa Claus traveled from his home
unit: Santa Claus traveled from his home accompanied by a band of Ryls and a dozen Knooks to attend Princess Ozma's birthday celebration in the Emerald City. Upon his arrival at the palace, he greeted Dorothy Gale and recognized Button-Bright, confirming he had visited the boy's home on Christmas Eves. He also promised Polychrome that he would inform her father, the Rainbow, of her location. Because he was getting fat and short of breath, Ozma allowed him to ride the Saw-Horse around the Emerald City to view the sights. At the royal banquet that evening, he sat in the seat of honor and gave a speech in verse wishing Ozma health and happiness. During the grand procession the next day, he rode the Saw-Horse while tossing small toys to the watching children. When the guests prepared to depart, Santa directed the Wizard of Oz in blowing giant magic bubbles to send foreign guests home, agreeing to take charge of Button-Bright's safe return. Finally, the Wizard blew a bubble around Santa Claus and his companions, and he floated away through the sky back to his home while waving to the cheering crowds.

label: History
value: The Saw-Horse was constructed out of wooden branches and a tree trunk.
unit: After being constructed out of wooden branches and a tree trunk, the Saw-Horse was brought to life by Tip using the Powder of Life. After Tip whittled wooden ears and attached them to its head, the Saw-Horse learned to hear and obey commands, acting as Jack Pumpkinhead's steed on their journey to the Emerald City. During their escapes and travels, it carried the party at great speed, swam across rivers, and helped carry sofa components up the palace to assemble the Flying Gump. It was instrumental in chasing down the Witch Mombi across the desert when she transformed into a Griffin, allowing Glinda to capture her. Following Princess Ozma's restoration to the throne, the Saw-Horse became her personal property and was fitted with golden shoes. It participated in the expedition to the Land of Ev, defeated Jim the Cab-horse in a race at Ozma's court, and served as a mount for dignitaries including the Scarecrow and Santa Claus.

label: History
value: The Scarecrow was taken off his pole in a Munchkin cornfield by Dorothy Gale.
unit: After being taken off his pole in a Munchkin cornfield by Dorothy Gale, the Scarecrow joined her journey to the Emerald City to ask the Wizard of Oz for brains. Along the way, he helped his companions navigate various dangers, fighting off the forty crows sent by the Wicked Witch of the West. When the Wizard was exposed as a humbug, he granted the Scarecrow brains made of bran mixed with pins and needles, and appointed him ruler of the Emerald City before departing in a balloon. Later, General Jinjur and her Army of Revolt overthrew the Scarecrow's reign; he escaped to seek aid from the Tin Woodman, Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, and Glinda the Good. During his journey, his straw was stolen by Jackdaws to build a nest, after which his body was re-stuffed with paper money. After Princess Ozma was restored to the throne of Oz, the Scarecrow relinquished his crown, was appointed Royal Treasurer by the Tin Woodman, and moved to live in the Tin Woodman's kingdom. Subsequently, he assisted Dorothy and Ozma on their expedition to Ev to rescue the Royal Family of Ev and the Tin Woodman from the Nome King.

label: Appearance
value: Shaggy Man has a shaggy appearance
unit: He has a shaggy appearance with shaggy hair, whiskers, clothes, and boots full of holes. Despite his untidy look, he has kind eyes, a pleasant twinkle, and a sweet smile. For a time, his head was transformed by magic into a shaggy, brown donkey head with large ears before being restored at the Truth Pond. In the Emerald City, he wears an elegant new costume made of rose-colored velvet, cream-colored satin, and ruby accessories, though deliberately styled with shags and bobtails to maintain his shaggy look.

label: History
value: The shaggy man asked Dorothy Gale for the road to Butterfield.
unit: While traveling in Kansas, the shaggy man asked Dorothy Gale for the road to Butterfield so he could avoid going there to prevent a man from paying back a fifteen-cent debt. He took apples from Dorothy's farm, hid Toto in his coat pocket, and led Dorothy onto a confusing junction of many strange roads, causing them both to get lost. Traveling together with Button-Bright and Polychrome, they encountered various unusual locations, including Foxville and Dunkonton, where King Kik-a-bray magically transformed the shaggy man's head into a donkey's head. After surviving an attack by the cannibalistic Scoodlers by catching their thrown heads and throwing them into a pit, he summoned Johnny Dooit with his Love Magnet to build a sand-boat, which allowed them to cross the Deadly Desert into the Land of Oz. Upon reaching Oz, he bathed in the Truth Pond to restore his human head, visited the Tin Woodman's castle, and traveled onward to the Emerald City. At Princess Ozma's palace, he admitted to having stolen the Love Magnet from an Eskimo, but was welcomed and gifted new, elegantly shaggy velvet attire. He attended Ozma's birthday celebration and was permitted to stay in Oz on condition that he remain honest and true.

He took apples from Dorothy's farm, hid Toto in his coat pocket, and led Dorothy onto a confusing junction of many strange roads, causing them both to get lost. Traveling together with Button-Bright and Polychrome, they encountered various unusual locations, including Foxville and Dunkonton, where King Kik-a-bray magically transformed the shaggy man's head into a donkey's head. After surviving an attack by the cannibalistic Scoodlers by catching their thrown heads and throwing them into a pit, he summoned Johnny Dooit with his Love Magnet to build a sand-boat, which allowed them to cross the Deadly Desert into the Land of Oz. Upon reaching Oz, he bathed in the Truth Pond to restore his human head, visited the Tin Woodman's castle, and traveled onward to the Emerald City. At Princess Ozma's palace, he admitted to having stolen the Love Magnet from an Eskimo, but was welcomed and gifted new, elegantly shaggy velvet attire. He attended Ozma's birthday celebration and was permitted to stay in Oz on condition that he remain honest and true.

label: History
value: An earthquake caused a Rain of Stones.
unit: When an earthquake caused a Rain of Stones and brought strangers into the underground Land of the Mangaboos, the Prince led Dorothy Gale and her companions to the Sorcerer to determine their innocence. The Sorcerer accused them of causing the damage and falsely predicted there would be no more rains from above. When the Wizard of Oz arrived in a balloon, the Prince arranged a magic contest between the Sorcerer and the Wizard. After the Wizard performed his piglet trick, Gwig attempted to kill the Wizard by stopping his breath with a magical spell. Before the magic could finish, the Wizard drew a jointed sword and sliced Gwig in two, revealing his vegetable interior. Following his defeat and cut condition, the Prince ordered Gwig's two halves to be taken to the public gardens and planted in a freshly plowed field so he could grow into a bush to produce new sorcerers.

label: History
value: Tiktok was invented in Ev-na.
unit: Tiktok was invented and manufactured in Ev-na by Smith & Tinker for King Evoldo of Ev. After being left locked in a rocky cavern, he was discovered by Dorothy Gale and Billina, who wound up his three separate clockworks for speech, action, and thought. He immediately declared himself Dorothy's obedient servant and protected her from the Wheelers using a tin dinner-pail. Upon guiding Dorothy to the royal palace of Ev, he knocked down several soldiers of Princess Langwidere before his action ran down. After being rewound, he joined Princess Ozma's expedition to rescue the royal family of Ev from the Nome King. In the Nome King's cavern, he was transformed into a gold ornament during the guessing game, but was restored by Ozma and Billina. Following their success, he accompanied Ozma to the Land of Oz, where Dorothy left him in Ozma's care. Residing at the Royal Palace in the Emerald City, he serves in ceremonial processions, greets arriving guests, and welcomes travelers on Ozma's behalf.

In the Nome King's cavern, he was transformed into a gold ornament during the guessing game, but was restored by Ozma and Billina. Following their success, he accompanied Ozma to the Land of Oz, where Dorothy left him in Ozma's care. Residing at the Royal Palace in the Emerald City, he serves in ceremonial processions, greets arriving guests, and welcomes travelers on Ozma's behalf.

label: Appearance
value: Tin Woodman is made entirely of tin.
unit: He is made entirely of tin, neatly soldered at the joints with cleverly hinged limbs that allow him to move as freely as flesh when properly oiled. He wears a funnel-shaped cap tipped carelessly over his left ear and carries a bright tin-plated axe set with diamonds over his shoulder. When freshly polished, his nickel-plated body sparkled brightly like silver, though he bears several soldered patches from repairs.

label: Personality
value: The Tin Woodman is remarkably polite.
unit: The Tin Woodman is remarkably polite, soft-hearted, and deeply considerate of every living creature. Lacking a natural heart at first, he exercised extreme care never to be cruel or unkind, weeping whenever he accidentally harmed even an insect. He is intensely loyal to his comrades and generous in hospitality, taking great pride in the happiness and content of others.

label: History
value: The Tin Woodman joined Dorothy and the Scarecrow's journey to the Emerald City
unit: After Dorothy and the Scarecrow oiled his rusted joints, the Tin Woodman joined their journey to the Emerald City to request a heart from the Wizard of Oz. Along the way, he cleared obstacles with his axe, fought off forty wolves sent by the Wicked Witch of the West, and was eventually smashed upon sharp rocks by the Winged Monkeys. He was repaired by the Winkie tinsmiths, and after helping defeat the Witch, he received a plush heart filled with sawdust from the Wizard. The grateful Winkies invited him to become their ruler, and he established a splendid tin palace in the Yellow Country of the West. He later marched to assist the Scarecrow against Jinjur's Army of Revolt, constructed the body of the flying Gump, and was briefly turned into a rose by Mombi. Subsequently, he led an army into the kingdom of the Nomes to assist Ozma in freeing the royal family of Ev, where he was temporarily transformed into an ornament before being restored. Later, he defended Dorothy's pet kitten Eureka during a formal trial in the Emerald City and welcomed Dorothy and her companions to his tin castle prior to Princess Ozma's birthday celebration.

label: History
value: Tip grew up in the Country of the Gillikins
unit: Tip grew up in the Country of the Gillikins under the care of Mombi, whom he disliked. To play a prank on her, he constructed a wooden man with a carved pumpkin head and named him Jack Pumpkinhead. After Mombi brought Jack to life using the Powder of Life, Tip overheard her plan to transform him into a marble statue, prompting him to run away at night with Jack and the remaining Powder of Life. During their journey to the Emerald City, Tip created ears for a wooden saw-horse and brought it to life with the powder to serve as Jack's mount. Upon encountering General Jinjur's Army of Revolt marching on the Emerald City, Tip warned the Scarecrow and helped him escape the besieged palace on the Saw-Horse. Joining forces with the Tin Woodman and the Woggle-Bug, Tip assisted in constructing a flying construct known as the Gump, bringing it to life with the final dose of the Powder of Life to escape capture. After traveling to the South Country to seek Glinda's aid, Tip accompanied Glinda's forces back to the Emerald City. Mombi was captured and revealed that Tip was actually Princess Ozma, whom she had transformed into a boy in infancy; Tip subsequently allowed Glinda to restore her to her original form.

Upon encountering General Jinjur's Army of Revolt marching on the Emerald City, Tip warned the Scarecrow and helped him escape the besieged palace on the Saw-Horse. Joining forces with the Tin Woodman and the Woggle-Bug, Tip assisted in constructing a flying construct known as the Gump, bringing it to life with the final dose of the Powder of Life to escape capture. After traveling to the South Country to seek Glinda's aid, Tip accompanied Glinda's forces back to the Emerald City. Mombi was captured and revealed that Tip was actually Princess Ozma, whom she had transformed into a boy in infancy; Tip subsequently allowed Glinda to restore her to her original form.

label: History
value: When a cyclone lifted Dorothy's house, Toto hid under the bed.
unit: When a cyclone lifted Dorothy's house, Toto hid under the bed and was nearly lost down the trap door before Dorothy rescued him, after which they were transported together to the Land of Oz. He accompanied Dorothy along the yellow brick road, forming friendships with the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, and the Cowardly Lion, whom he bravely defended when it first confronted them. After defeating the Wicked Witch of the West and visiting Glinda the Good, Toto returned with Dorothy to Kansas when she used the Silver Shoes. Later, Toto was trapped briefly in the shaggy man's pocket after biting his finger on the farm, leading him to join Dorothy, the shaggy man, Button-Bright, and Polychrome on a journey through strange lands to Oz. During their travels, he helped battle Scoodlers by stealing one of their heads and safely crossed the Deadly Desert on a sand-boat. Reaching the Emerald City, he attended Princess Ozma's birthday celebration and was transported back home to Kansas alongside Dorothy via the Magic Belt.

unit: Uncle Henry is a stern, solemn, and quiet man who rarely speaks and works hard from morning until night. He does not know what joy is and never laughs. However, he cares deeply for his niece, Dorothy, and feels sad and lonely when she is lost.

label: History
value: Uncle Henry lived on a small farm in Kansas.
unit: Uncle Henry lived on a small farm in Kansas with his wife, Aunt Em, and his orphaned niece, Dorothy Gale. After a powerful cyclone destroyed their house and took Dorothy away, he constructed a new farmhouse and resumed his farming duties. His health eventually broke down from continuous hard work, leading him to take Dorothy on a voyage to Australia to visit relatives and recover while Aunt Em managed the Kansas farm. During a violent ocean storm on their trip, Dorothy went missing, which deeply saddened Uncle Henry and further impaired his health while he stayed in Sydney. Once Dorothy safely returned to him in Australia via magic, his condition immediately began to improve. Later, after returning to Kansas, he went into mourning when he mistakenly believed Dorothy had been killed in a California earthquake, but she eventually returned home once more.

label: History
value: The Wicked Witch of the West leagued with three other witches.
unit: The Wicked Witch of the West leagued with three other witches to depose the king of Oz and divide the land among themselves. Using the magic Golden Cap, she summoned the Winged Monkeys to conquer and enslave the yellow Winkies in the West Country and later to drive the Wizard of Oz out of her territory. When Dorothy Gale and her friends traveled West to destroy her, the Witch sent packs of wolves, flocks of crows, swarms of bees, and Winkie soldiers against them, all of which failed. She then used the final charge of her Golden Cap to send the Winged Monkeys to destroy the Tin Woodman and Scarecrow, capture the Cowardly Lion, and bring Dorothy to her castle. She forced Dorothy to work in her kitchen and tried to starve the Lion into drawing her chariot. Cunningly using an invisible iron bar to trip Dorothy, she stole one of her Silver Shoes. When an angry Dorothy threw a bucket of water over her, the Wicked Witch completely melted away, ending her reign of evil.

label: History
value: The Wizard refused to see Dorothy and her companions face to face.
unit: When Dorothy and her companions first reached the Emerald City to ask for aid, the Wizard refused to see them face to face, using paper heads, fire, and other illusions to conceal his true form. After Dorothy melted the Wicked Witch of the West, Toto accidentally knocked down a screen in the throne room, exposing the Wizard as a common old man from Omaha who relied on mechanical tricks and ventriloquism. Unable to perform real magic, he nevertheless satisfied Dorothy's companions by granting them symbolic tokens of brains, a heart, and courage. He attempted to carry Dorothy back to Kansas in a hot-air balloon, but the ropes snapped prematurely and he was carried away alone, leaving the Scarecrow in charge of the city. He returned to working in a circus until an earthquake swallowed him along with a horse, a buggy, and Dorothy into the underground world. After escaping subterranean dangers with the group, he was brought to the Emerald City via Princess Ozma's Magic Belt. Upon his return, Princess Ozma welcomed him warmly and appointed him the Official Wizard of Oz. In his new position, he entertains the court with sleight-of-hand piglet tricks, bubble inventions, and magic performances.

After Dorothy melted the Wicked Witch of the West, Toto accidentally knocked down a screen in the throne room, exposing the Wizard as a common old man from Omaha who relied on mechanical tricks and ventriloquism. Unable to perform real magic, he nevertheless satisfied Dorothy's companions by granting them symbolic tokens of brains, a heart, and courage. He attempted to carry Dorothy back to Kansas in a hot-air balloon, but the ropes snapped prematurely and he was carried away alone, leaving the Scarecrow in charge of the city. He returned to working in a circus until an earthquake swallowed him along with a horse, a buggy, and Dorothy into the underground world. After escaping subterranean dangers with the group, he was brought to the Emerald City via Princess Ozma's Magic Belt. Upon his return, Princess Ozma welcomed him warmly and appointed him the Official Wizard of Oz. In his new position, he entertains the court with sleight-of-hand piglet tricks, bubble inventions, and magic performances.

label: Quotes
value: > It affords me great pleasure to surprise people; for surely I cannot be classed with ordinary insects and am entitled to both curiosity and admiration from those I meet.

label: Quotes
value: > H. M... means Highly Magnified; and T. E. means Thoroughly Educated. I am, in reality, a very big bug, and doubtless the most intelligent being in all this broad domain.

label: Appearance
value: The Woggle-Bug is a greatly enlarged insect.
unit: The Woggle-Bug is a greatly enlarged insect, fully as tall as a man, with a round dark-brown body striped on the front with light brown and white. He stands upright on slender legs ending in delicate curling feet, and his head features bulging round black eyes and antennae on his ears and nose. For clothing, he wears a dark-blue swallowtail coat with a yellow silk lining, a tight white duck vest, fawn-colored plush knickerbockers with gilt buckles, and a tall silk hat.

label: History
value: The Woggle-Bug encountered Tip.
unit: While wandering through Oz, the Woggle-Bug encountered Tip, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Jack Pumpkinhead, and the Saw-Horse, and joined them on their journey to the Emerald City. Along the way, he irritated his companions with constant puns until warned by the Tin Woodman. Upon reaching the Emerald City, Queen Jinjur captured the group and threatened to turn the Woggle-Bug into goulash or soup, but they escaped to the roof and constructed the Gump to fly away. After crashing into a nest of Jackdaws—who are the natural enemies of his race—the Woggle-Bug was hidden under the Scarecrow's straw, swallowed a Wishing Pill to mend the Gump's wings, and escaped with the group to Glinda's palace. He accompanied Glinda's army to liberate the Emerald City, where Queen Ozma appointed him Public Educator and later built the College of Art and Athletic Perfection, making him its Dean and President. During a trial in the Emerald City, he served as Public Accuser against Dorothy's kitten Eureka. Later, he composed and read an 'Ode to Ozma' at her birthday celebration.

Along the way, he irritated his companions with constant puns until warned by the Tin Woodman. Upon reaching the Emerald City, Queen Jinjur captured the group and threatened to turn the Woggle-Bug into goulash or soup, but they escaped to the roof and constructed the Gump to fly away. After crashing into a nest of Jackdaws—who are the natural enemies of his race—the Woggle-Bug was hidden under the Scarecrow's straw, swallowed a Wishing Pill to mend the Gump's wings, and escaped with the group to Glinda's palace. He accompanied Glinda's army to liberate the Emerald City, where Queen Ozma appointed him Public Educator and later built the College of Art and Athletic Perfection, making him its Dean and President. During a trial in the Emerald City, he served as Public Accuser against Dorothy's kitten Eureka. Later, he composed and read an 'Ode to Ozma' at her birthday celebration.

label: Personality
value: Zeb is hardworking.
unit: Zeb is a hardworking, polite, and confident worker who considers himself a splendid hand at his job. Though prone to fear and anxiety when faced with strange and dangerous magical situations, he pushes past his hesitation so as not to appear cowardly. He displays resourcefulness and bravery during crises, readily taking up improvised weapons to defend his companions. He can also be playfully mischievous, such as teasing Jim the Cab-Horse, though he remains respectful and appreciative of others.

label: History
value: Zeb was driving Jim the Cab-Horse.
unit: Zeb was driving Jim the Cab-Horse to pick up Dorothy Gale when a severe earthquake swallowed the horse, buggy, and children into the earth. They fell into the underground Land of the Mangaboos, where they were accused of causing damage by a rain of stones. After meeting the Wizard of Oz, the group was walled up in a glass mountain by the vegetable people, but they escaped through a subterranean tunnel to the Valley of Voe. Threatened by invisible bears, they walked across a river using magic leaves and climbed a spiral staircase inside Pyramid Mountain to the wooden Country of the Gargoyles. When attacked by the Gargoyles, Zeb fought bravely using a captured Gargoyle king as a club, and later descended a rope made of harness straps to steal wooden wings that enabled their escape. Following further travels through dangerous underground caverns, Dorothy used Princess Ozma's Magic Belt to transport Zeb, the Wizard, Jim, and the rest of their companions safely to the Emerald City. While enjoying his stay in Oz, Zeb participated in athletic games, wrestled a Munchkin champion, and served as a juror during the trial of Eureka the kitten. Desiring to return to his normal life, Zeb was eventually transported back to Hugson's Ranch by Princess Ozma's magic belt.
